```{r}
#| label: load-data

library(ggplot2)
library(ggrain)

h1Data <- read.csv("data/processed_data/practice_h1.csv")
h1Data$Sex_birth <- factor(h1Data$Sex_birth,
                           levels = c("Male", "Female", "Intersex"))
h2Data <- read.csv("data/processed_data/practice_h2.csv")
```

## Hypothesis 1

Points allocated to a partner's physical attractiveness differ by sex at
birth.

### Variables and descriptive statistics

- **Sex at birth (`Sex_birth`):** A categorical variable with three
  groups: Male, Female, and Intersex.
- **Importance of partner physical attractiveness
  (`preference_imp_physat`):** Points allocated to physical
  attractiveness from a total budget of 30 points across six partner
  characteristics. Higher values indicate greater relative importance.

"\*\*" makes text bold "\`\`" will show things in a more "code" way

```{r}
#| label: h1-descriptives
# Count respondents in each group.
table(h1Data$Sex_birth)

# Summarize attractiveness points separately for each group.
by(h1Data$preference_imp_physat, h1Data$Sex_birth, summary)
# by function lets me put summary by groups 
# by works with table etc as well

```

### Graph

@fig-attractiveness shows the distribution of points by sex at birth.
The half-violin shows the shape of the distribution, the box summarizes
the median and quartiles, and the dots represent individual responses.

@fig-attractiveness links to the code chunk in this case to #\| label:
fig-attractiveness below

```{r}
#| label: fig-attractiveness
#| fig-cap: "Points allocated to a partner's physical attractiveness, by sex at birth."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

# above I can adjust width and height of figure and figure description! 

ggplot(h1Data, aes(x = Sex_birth, y = preference_imp_physat,
                   fill = Sex_birth)) +
  geom_rain(alpha = 0.5, point.args = list(alpha = 0.04, size = 0.6)) +
  labs(x = "Sex at birth", y = "Points allocated to physical attractiveness") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## H2. Confidence in finding a new partner and commitment

Confidence in finding a new partner is associated with relationship
commitment.

### Variables and descriptive statistics

- **Confidence in finding a new partner (`qoa`):** A single item about
  finding another appealing partner if the current relationship ended.
  Responses range from 1 (Strongly disagree) to 7 (Strongly agree).
- **Relationship commitment (`commitment`):** The mean of available
  responses to `prqc_4`, `prqc_5`, and `prqc_6`. Each item ranges from 1
  (Not at all) to 7 (Extremely); higher scores indicate greater
  commitment.

This dataset includes respondents who were dating, in a committed
relationship, or married.

```{r}
#| label: h2-descriptives
summary(h2Data[, c("qoa", "commitment")])
```

### Graph

@fig-commitment shows the relationship between confidence and
commitment. Points are jittered to make overlapping responses easier to
see; the recorded scores are unchanged. The line summarizes the linear
trend.

```{r}
#| label: fig-commitment
#| fig-cap: "Confidence in finding a new partner and relationship commitment."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

ggplot(h2Data, aes(x = qoa, y = commitment)) +
  geom_jitter(width = .12, height = .04, alpha = .04, size = .6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  labs(x = "Confidence in finding a new partner (1–7)",
       y = "Relationship commitment (1–7)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

### Observed trend

```{r}
#| label: correlation
r <- cor(h2Data$qoa, h2Data$commitment, use = "complete.obs")
round(r, 2)
```

The correlation was `{r} round(r, 2)`, indicating a weak negative
association. Respondents who reported more confidence in finding a new
partner tended to report lower commitment.
